Preparing your globeNatural Earth II imagery

DIRECT GEOMETRY EDITING

A globe. Your geometry.

Circle
Choose Circle and click the globe to place its centre. Drag the centre to move it, or the edge handle to resize it. Radius is measured over the WGS 84 ellipsoid.
Polygon
Click to add vertices. Fill appears at three points. Double-click, press Enter, or choose Finish to close the polygon. Drag the gold MOVE handle near the middle of a selected polygon to move the entire shape around the globe. Drag its solid handles to edit; click hollow midpoint handles to insert a vertex. Click overlapping shapes to choose one from a popup menu.
Views
Globe shows the 3D Earth, Flat shows a 2D map, and 2.5D shows a tilted flat map. Shapes and selections stay available across views. Finish or cancel a draft polygon before switching.
Navigate & manage
Drag empty globe to orbit. Scroll or pinch to zoom. V selects, C draws a circle, P draws a polygon. Escape cancels drawing or deselects. Delete removes the selected shape. Click the shape count to browse all completed shapes and fly to one. Shape names appear on the globe; select one to rename it. Shift/Ctrl/Cmd-click or use Multi to toggle several shapes, including in the shape list. Select exactly two overlapping shapes and choose Merge into polygon. Disconnected results and holes are rejected. Crossing-edge edits revert automatically. Undo/Redo restores completed edits (Ctrl/Cmd+Z; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z). Drawings save on this browser.
Imagery: Natural Earth II (public domain). Globe: CesiumJS 1.121.0. Geometry: polygon-clipping and GeographicLib (MIT; notices). Natural Earth is a low-resolution global basemap; zooming in does not add street-level detail.
